summary_oneline: PythonREPL WorkerPool death spiral: PythonPandasTool seeds each fresh worker through the hard-coded 5 s namespace API, which SIGKILLs a worker that is still bootstrapping, so every call kills the next spare before it is ready

localization.role: single request/response gate; on asyncio.wait_for timeout it SIGKILLs the worker and re-raises a bare TimeoutError
namespace API with a hard-coded 5.0 s timeout and no error handling (vs 60.25 s for execute, 30 s for inject_dataframe, 10 s for ping)
spawns the child and returns immediately — no readiness handshake
existing 10 s health check whose docstring acknowledges multi-second bootstrap; never called anywhere
appends a spare and logs 'prewarmed worker ready' right after Popen; the spare is not warm
crash-restart: replaces a dead session worker with the OLDEST spare (pop(0)) using is_alive as the only health signal
child cannot answer any frame until the full parrot + pandas import and PythonREPLTool bootstrap finish; no 'ready' frame is sent
re-seeds df_locals into every new WorkerHandle: DataFrames via inject_dataframe (30 s), scalars via set_var (5 s), in set-iteration order
adds four scalar metadata entries per DataFrame name and per alias to df_locals — the set_var seeding load
calls list_vars before and list_vars/get_var after every execution inside try/except — failures are swallowed but each timeout has already killed the worker
log sites :945/:960; converts any escaping exception into {status:'error', error:str(e)} — blank for TimeoutError
raise ValueError(result.error) — produces the reported empty ValueError
deadline_ms=60000, prewarm_pool_size=2; no field for namespace-API timeout or bootstrap grace

constraints.statement: Namespace-API timeouts are hard-coded 5.0 s in handle.py and not exposed through WorkerConfig
constraints.implication: no deployment-side knob exists to mitigate; the fix must change code, not config

constraints.statement: _send() kills the worker on ANY timeout, including namespace calls, and re-raises a bare TimeoutError whose str() is empty
constraints.implication: a fix must decide whether a namespace timeout should still be lethal, and must give the error a message either way

constraints.statement: PythonPandasTool re-seeds all df_locals on every new handle identity, before the caller's own request
constraints.implication: any readiness fix must cover the seeding path, not only execute(); seeding order is hash-dependent and must not be relied upon

constraints.statement: The G5 error contract for execute() returns a dict, never raises; the loss-error path assumes the worker died DURING an exec
constraints.implication: a worker killed by a namespace timeout currently produces an exception path with no lost-variables message — the fix should route it into the same G5 contract

constraints.statement: WorkerHandle.ping() already exists (10 s) but is dead code; test_integration.py documents the cold-start hazard for deadline_ms only
constraints.implication: a readiness handshake can reuse ping(); a cold-start regression test is missing and must be added

constraints.statement: Worker bootstrap costs ≈2.4 s idle (1.74 s of it is importing parrot.tools.pythonrepl) and 12-14 s under 3× CPU oversubscription; 3 workers boot concurrently by default
constraints.implication: 5 s is inside the normal variance of production hosts; the spare pool itself adds boot contention

constraints.statement: origin/main and dev are identical on all affected files; last change 2026-08-20, core logic from 2026-07-28
constraints.implication: not a regression; a hotfix based on main is viable and propagates via sync-down

constraints.statement: Other callers share the same 5 s namespace API: PandasAgent get_var/snapshot, working-memory snapshot wiring, tools/agent.py set_var
constraints.implication: the fix belongs in handle.py/pool.py (shared layer), not in PythonPandasTool alone

constraints.statement: Worker bootstrap import is dominated by the parrot framework init (navconfig/vault/documentdb/events/navigator auth ≈80 %), not by pandas (≈16 %)
constraints.implication: a readiness handshake fixes the spiral; trimming the worker's import surface is a valid, separate follow-up that also shrinks prewarm cost

hypotheses.statement: A fresh worker is handed out before it finishes bootstrapping; PythonPandasTool's first message to it is a set_var with a 5 s timeout, the timeout SIGKILLs the still-booting worker and raises a blank TimeoutError, and the pool then binds the next spare — which was spawned only 5 s earlier — so the cycle repeats indefinitely while bootstrap stays above 5 s.
hypotheses.reasoning: Reproduced on dev with the report's exact log lines, 5 s cadence, blank error text and error dict (F016). Every element is directly cited: no readiness check (F003/F004), 5 s hard-coded timeouts (F004), kill-on-timeout (F004), seeding on the new-handle path (F009), and blank str(TimeoutError) (F017).
hypotheses.next_probe: On the affected host, capture the worker's own stdout via the drain logger (`repl_worker[pid=… stdout]`) and measure spawn→`repl_worker: ready`; confirm it exceeds 5 s. Also confirm the initial trigger of the first death (TTL eviction, deadline kill, or the same cold-start timeout on first use).

hypotheses.statement: The very first worker death in the reported session had a different cause (idle-TTL eviction after 30 min, a 60 s exec deadline kill, or a memory/rlimit crash), and the cold-start spiral is only the failure to RECOVER from it.
hypotheses.reasoning: The report starts mid-spiral ('worker is dead, restarting' is the first line), so the initial trigger is unobserved. It does not change the fix: recovery is broken regardless of what killed the first worker, and on a slow host the first-ever use also enters the spiral (F016 Probe B).
hypotheses.next_probe: Search the full server log for the first `worker is dead` / `evicting idle session` / `REPL worker terminated (` line for that session id.

hypotheses.statement: Production bootstrap is slower than the idle baseline because the worker re-runs the full parrot package init (navconfig env/vault load, logstash handler, tool-registry import) on every spawn, and 3 workers boot concurrently per tool instance.
hypotheses.reasoning: Measured: 1.95 s to reach the parrot package init and 2.4 s to ready on an idle 12-core box, 12-14 s under contention. Production specifics (vault, logstash, container CPU quota) are unmeasured.
hypotheses.next_probe: Run `python -X importtime -c 'from parrot.tools.pythonrepl import PythonREPLTool'` on the affected host and inspect the top offenders.

confidence_map.statement: WorkerHandle.start() and WorkerPool._top_up_prewarmed() perform no readiness check; a spare is marked ready in the same millisecond it is spawned
confidence_map.reasoning: direct read of both functions; matches the report's same-millisecond spawn/ready log pair

confidence_map.statement: get_var/set_var/list_vars use a hard-coded 5.0 s timeout and _send() SIGKILLs the worker on timeout
PythonPandasTool re-seeds df_locals via set_var/inject_dataframe on every new WorkerHandle identity, before the caller's request
The blank error text and ValueError type are str(TimeoutError()) == '' propagated through pythonrepl.py:960 → ToolResult.error → base.py raise ValueError(result.error)
confidence_map.reasoning: each hop read directly; verified empty str on Python 3.12

confidence_map.statement: The report's log signature is reproducible on dev by seeding one scalar into a cold worker under CPU load
confidence_map.reasoning: Probe B output matches line numbers, cadence, blank text and the returned error dict

confidence_map.statement: Whether a call survives depends on set-iteration order of df_locals (DataFrame first → 30 s budget, scalar first → 5 s)
confidence_map.reasoning: Probe A vs Probe B differ only in which value type is seeded first

confidence_map.statement: Worker bootstrap takes ≈2.4 s idle and 12-14 s under 3× CPU oversubscription on the dev machine
confidence_map.reasoning: measured from the worker's own ready log via the drain task

confidence_map.statement: This is not a code regression; affected code is unchanged since 2026-08-20 and identical on main
confidence_map.reasoning: git log and diff --stat read directly

confidence_map.statement: ping() is unused and no test covers the namespace API against a cold worker
The initial death of the reported session's first worker was caused by the same cold-start timeout

confidence_map.statement: On the dev box, ~80 % of the worker's 1.41 s import is parrot framework init (navconfig, vault utils, documentdb, events, navigator auth); pandas is ~16 %
confidence_map.reasoning: measured with python -X importtime; host-side share (network-bound navconfig) still unmeasured

unknowns.question: Should this ship as a hotfix based on main (the bug is in the released code, F013) or as a feature-flow fix on dev?
plausible_answers: hotfix — base main, propagate via sync-down (recommended: production agents are unusable)
feature on dev — ride the next release
unknowns.user_answer: feature flow on dev — the bug is on dev (and main); ship in the next release, not as a hotfix

unknowns.question: When a namespace-API call (set_var/get_var/list_vars) times out on an otherwise-alive worker, should the worker still be SIGKILLed (current behaviour) or left alive with the call failing softly?
plausible_answers: keep lethal, but only after readiness is confirmed (timeouts then mean a real hang)
make namespace timeouts non-lethal; only execute() deadline kills
raise the namespace timeout to deadline_ms and keep lethal
unknowns.user_answer: execute deadline kill only — namespace-API timeouts must not SIGKILL the worker

unknowns.question: On the affected host, how long does a worker take from spawn to `repl_worker: ready`, and what dominates (navconfig/vault/logstash init vs pandas import vs CPU quota)?
plausible_answers: > 5 s mostly from parrot package init (navconfig/vault/logstash) — worth trimming the worker's import surface
> 5 s from CPU contention (many agents / spares booting at once) — readiness handshake alone suffices
< 5 s normally; the incident coincided with a load spike
unknowns.user_answer: unknown to the user; research required. Local importtime profile added as F018 (parrot framework init ≈80 % of bootstrap, pandas ≈16 %); the affected host still needs measuring — carry a probe task into the spec

recommended_next_command.rationale: Root cause is reproduced and localized to handle.py/pool.py with high confidence; the remaining choices (readiness handshake via ping vs. timeout budget, lethal vs. soft namespace timeouts, hotfix base) are bounded design decisions best captured in a spec, not an open architectural fork.
